resumen: have / get + objeto + participio: otra persona hace el trabajo por nosotros: I had my hair cut., I'm going to get my car serviced. (I cut my hair = me lo corté yo).
Tiempos: solo cambia have/get y el participio queda igual: We're getting the office painted., Have you had it redecorated?
Experiencias negativas: have something done también cuenta lo que otros nos hicieron: We had our car stolen. = nos robaron el coche.
have + persona + infinitivo sin to (encargar una tarea): I'll have the technician check it.; get + persona + to (convencer): I got my brother to help.
make / let + objeto + infinitivo sin to: She made me practise., They let me use the car.; help admite ambos (help me (to) move), nunca -ing.
Pasiva de make: recupera el to: We were made to wear a tie.; let no tiene pasiva: se dice we were allowed to.
need + -ing tiene sentido pasivo: The windows need cleaning. = need to be cleaned.

preguntas.q: Do you like my hair? I didn't cut it myself; I ___ at the new salon near the office.
preguntas.x: Have something done indica que otra persona hizo el trabajo: I had it cut = me lo cortaron. I cut it diría que lo hice yo, y had cut it es past perfect, no causativa: en la causativa el objeto va antes del participio.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “A mechanic is going to service my car tomorrow.”
preguntas.a: I'm going to get my car serviced tomorrow.
d: I'm going to service my car tomorrow.
I'm going to get serviced my car tomorrow.
I'm going to get my car to service tomorrow.
preguntas.x: Get/have + objeto + participio: get my car serviced = que me lo revisen. I'm going to service my car significa que lo haré yo, y en la causativa el objeto va siempre antes del participio.

preguntas.q: My parents let me ___ the car at weekends if I help my dad ___ the garden.
preguntas.x: Let + objeto + infinitivo sin to: let me use. Help + objeto admite infinitivo con o sin to (help my dad clean o to clean), pero nunca -ing.

preguntas.q: After a lot of persuading, I finally ___ my brother to help me paint the living room.
preguntas.x: De los verbos causativos, solo get lleva to: get someone to do = «conseguir que alguien haga algo», normalmente convenciéndolo. Make y let van con infinitivo sin to, y manage no admite objeto (I managed to paint it).

preguntas.a: My piano teacher made me practise the same piece twenty times.
d: My piano teacher made me to practise the same piece twenty times.
My piano teacher made me practising the same piece twenty times.
My piano teacher made that I practised the same piece twenty times.
preguntas.x: Make + objeto + infinitivo sin to = obligar a alguien: made me practise. Made me to practise es el error más común, y made that I practised calca «hizo que practicara».

preguntas.q: Decorators are in our office this week: we're ___, so we're all working from home.
preguntas.x: La causativa admite cualquier tiempo cambiando solo get/have: we're getting it painted (presente continuo). El objeto va antes del participio, y get it to paint diría que la oficina va a pintar algo.

preguntas.q: When I was at secondary school, we ___ wear a tie every single day.
preguntas.x: En pasiva, make recupera el to: we were made to wear a tie (= nos obligaban). Let no se usa en pasiva así; se diría we were allowed to.

preguntas.q: The windows are filthy after the storm; they really need ___.
preguntas.x: Need + -ing tiene sentido pasivo: they need cleaning = they need to be cleaned. They need to clean diría que las ventanas tienen que limpiar algo.

preguntas.q: We ___ last night while we were at the cinema, so we had to get a taxi home.
preguntas.x: Have something done también describe algo desagradable que nos hacen otros: We had our car stolen = nos robaron el coche. We had stolen our car es past perfect y diría que lo robamos nosotros.

preguntas.q: The kitchen looks fantastic! ___ it redecorated?
preguntas.x: En present perfect, la causativa repite have: Have you had it redecorated? (el primero es auxiliar y el segundo, el verbo causativo). Have you it redecorated? omite el verbo principal.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “I persuaded my landlord to fix the heating.”
preguntas.a: I got my landlord to fix the heating.
d: I got my landlord fix the heating.
I made my landlord to fix the heating.
I let my landlord fix the heating.
preguntas.x: Get someone to do something = «convencer a alguien de que haga algo», el sentido de persuade. Con get el to es obligatorio, make no lo lleva, y let significa «permitir», no «convencer».

preguntas.a: I'll have the technician check your laptop this afternoon.
d: I'll have the technician checked your laptop this afternoon.
I'll get the technician check your laptop this afternoon.
I'll have checked your laptop by the technician this afternoon.
preguntas.x: Have + persona + infinitivo sin to = encargarle una tarea a alguien: have the technician check it. El participio solo va con la cosa (have your laptop checked), y con get haría falta to: get the technician to check.
